key_insight: OmniShow unifies text, reference images, audio, and pose into a single conditioning framework to synthesize controllable, high-quality human–object interaction videos, enabling rich multimodal guidance for video generation.
problem_solved: Existing HOI video generation methods cannot simultaneously accept and reconcile all practical conditioning signals (text, appearance references, audio, and pose), limiting controllability and real-world applicability for tasks like e‑commerce demos and short video production.
method: Unified multimodal conditioning pipeline that accepts text, reference images, audio, and pose as complementary controls for video synthesis.
Modality-specific encoders and a cross-modal fusion module to integrate semantics (text), appearance (images), sound (audio), and motion (pose) into a shared representation.
Temporal synthesis and object-centric rendering components to ensure motion coherence and consistent human–object interactions across generated frames.
impact: OmniShow gives practitioners a practical blueprint for building flexible, controllable HOI video generators that can be steered by multiple real-world signals, accelerating content automation for commerce, entertainment, and interactive applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: modality encoders (text/image/audio/pose) → fusion module → temporal video decoder
Input-to-output panel: combined inputs (text, reference image, audio waveform, pose sequence) mapped to generated video frames
Timeline/motion visualization: frame sequence showing temporal coherence and aligned pose-driven motion
Comparison strip: side-by-side qualitative comparisons to prior single-condition methods (emphasizing improved control and realism)
paper_title: OmniShow: Unifying Multimodal Conditions for Human-Object Interaction Video Generation
paper_authors: Donghao Zhou, Guisheng Liu, Hao Yang, Jiatong Li, Jingyu Lin
